title: Complaints commission reviewing RCMP's handling of Alberta woman who died in cell
article: The RCMP watchdog is not waiting for a complaint to start reviewing the actions of officers following the death of a woman in custody in a northern Alberta detachment.
Ian McPail, the interim chair of the Commission for Public Complaints Against the RCMP, has initiated the review on his own.
Commission spokesman Jamie Robertson said Thursday the fact that the woman died in a police holding cell is enough to warrant the independent investigation.
"We weren't just going to wait for a complaint. We made the call that this was a prudent thing to do."
Robertson added 28-year-old Charlene Danais is the first person to die in custody since June, when the commission released its scathing report into case of Raymond Silverfox of Whitehorse.

Silverfox, arrested for drunkenness, repeatedly vomited and soiled himself during his 13-hour stint in an RCMP cell. A coroner determined he died of natural causes - one factor being an acute infection as a result of breathing his own vomit.

The commission ruled Mounties and guards on duty failed to properly supervise and assess Silverfox. In its final report, the agency committed to annual reviews of similar incidents for the next three years.

Marilyn Danais said her daughter and son-in-law, Brent Providence, were drunk last Saturday. So she called RCMP to handle them for the night at the local detachment in Assumption, a remote community tucked into the northwest corner of the province, about 900 kilometres from Edmonton.
Officers placed the couple in different cells. Providence said he was concerned about his wife's health because she had earlier taken anti-depressants and sleeping pills.
"I told the cops to check on her. She took some pills, but I didn't see it," he said.
RCMP spokesman Sgt. Patrick Webb said Danais did not appear injured and co-operated with officers when she was arrested for mischief and taken to the detachment.
Eight hours later, officers found her in her cell not breathing. She was later pronounced dead at the hospital in High Level.
Providence said he told officers the next morning he wanted to wait there for his wife. After 22 hours in his cell, they took him to a room and told him she had died, he said.
Mounties should have done more to help his wife get medical attention, he said.
The couple, married 10 years, have two children. Danais worked as a teacher's assistant.
An autopsy could not determine the woman's cause of death and toxicology results are not expected for several months.
Alberta's fatality review board automatically reviews the deaths of people in police custody.
RCMP in Peace River are also investigating what happened. Webb said they will be interviewing family members and reviewing video surveillance from the holding cell area.
